description: A shallow tree of fixed-size sorted pages updated in place; fast point reads and range scans, random writes for random keys.
An append-only log that makes each change durable before it is acknowledged, replayed after a crash to rebuild what only memory held.
The sorted in-memory structure of an LSM tree that takes every new write until it is flushed.
An immutable file of key-value entries sorted by key, produced by a MemTable flush or by compaction.
A compact bit array that says a key is definitely absent or maybe present, letting reads skip SSTables without disk access.
A delete marker written as a new entry; it hides older values until compaction removes both.
Merging SSTables into fewer files that keep only the newest version of each key, trading disk work for faster reads and less space.
Disk reads per lookup, bytes written per byte of data and disk used per byte of live data: the three costs every engine trades.
